claim: SRSF10 is essential for spermatogenesis and male fertility.

claim: There was no difference in germ cell numbers between control and Srsf10-cKO testes at P3.

claim: The number of PLZF+ undifferentiated spermatogonia was gradually increased in both control and Srsf10-cKO testes from P3 to P12.

claim: The kinetics of PLZF+ cell increase in Srsf10-cKO testes was much slower than in control testes.

claim: The expression of PLZF in P3 testes was lower, and no significant difference was observed between control and Srsf10-cKO testes.

claim: The expression of PLZF was apparently increased from P3 to P8 in control testes but was only slightly increased in Srsf10-cKO testes.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1C showing western blot data.

claim: Srsf10 may be essential for the expansion of the progenitor spermatogonia population.
source: All these data suggest that Srsf10 may be essential for the expansion of the progenitor spermatogonia population, disturbance of which may further lead to differentiation defect.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Only 10 upregulated and 9 downregulated genes were identified in Srsf10-cKO testes compared with the control at P3.
source: RNA-seq analyses identified only 10 upregulated and 9 downregulated genes in Srsf10-cKO testes compared with the control at P3 ( fragments per kilobase of exon per million reads mapped [FPKM] ≥5, fold change ≥2, and p<0.01; Figure 4A), suggesting that the transcriptome is largely normal at P3 in Srsf10-depleted testes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A showing RNA-seq data.

claim: The transcriptome is largely normal at P3 in Srsf10-depleted testes.
source: RNA-seq analyses identified only 10 upregulated and 9 downregulated genes in Srsf10-cKO testes compared with the control at P3 ( fragments per kilobase of exon per million reads mapped [FPKM] ≥5, fold change ≥2, and p<0.01; Figure 4A), suggesting that the transcriptome is largely normal at P3 in Srsf10-depleted testes.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the results section based on RNA-seq data.

claim: 138 genes were differentially expressed between the control and Srsf10-cKO testes at P6.

claim: Nearly all genes (135/138) differentially expressed at P6 were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes.
source: However, 138 genes were differentially expressed between the control and Srsf10-cKO testes at P6, and nearly all genes (135/138) were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A showing RNA-seq data.

claim: 396 genes were differentially expressed in Srsf10-cKO testes at P8, including 243 upregulated and 153 downregulated genes.
source: 396 genes were differentially expressed in Srsf10-cKO testes at P8, including 243 upregulated and 153 downregulated genes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4A showing RNA-seq data.

claim: Only 57 genes were commonly downregulated in the Srsf10-cKO testes at both P6 and P8.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4B showing Venn diagram.

claim: The 57 commonly downregulated genes are involved in the meiotic cell cycle, spermatogenesis, cell differentiation, and germ cell development.
source: GO analysis of the 57 genes showed that these genes are involved in the meiotic cell cycle, spermatogenesis, cell differentiation, and germ cell development (Figure 4B).

claim: The vast majority of downregulated genes were gradually increased from P3 to P8 in control testes.

claim: Many genes that were only significantly downregulated at P6 were mainly involved in the expansion and early differentiation of progenitor spermatogonia.
source: Interestingly, many genes that were only significantly downregulated at P6 (e.g. Pou5f1, Sohlh1, Egr4, Nanos3, Foxc2, and Sox3) were mainly involved in the expansion and early differentiation of progenitor spermatogonia (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4B showing gene lists.

claim: Many genes that were only significantly downregulated at P8 were involved in spermatogonia differentiation and meiosis.
source: Many genes that were only significantly downregulated at P8 (e.g. Kit, Sycp3, Sycp2, Atm, and Rec8) were involved in spermatogonia differentiation and meiosis and were barely upregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes from P6 to P8 (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), echoing nearly no differentiating spermatogonia and meiotic spermatocytes in P8 Srsf10-cKO testes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The gene expression pattern of Srsf10-cKO testes at P8 was much more similar to that of control testes at P6.
source: Unsupervised cluster analysis of spermatogonia-specific genes (SPGs; Green et al., 2018) showed that the gene expression pattern of Srsf10-cKO testes at P8 was much more similar to that of control testes at P6 (Figure 4C), consistent with the compromised and slower expansion and differentiation of progenitor spermatogonia in the Srsf10-cKO testes than control.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4C showing hierarchical clustering.

claim: Most genes involved in SSCs maintenance were hardly affected in the Srsf10-cKO testes from P3 to P8.
source: Most genes involved in SSCs maintenance (Etv5, Bmi1, Id4, Lhx1, Cd82, and T) were hardly affected in the Srsf10-cKO testes from P3 to P8.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Genes associated with progenitor spermatogonia were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes at P6 and P8 compared to control.
source: However, genes associated with progenitor spermatogonia (Lin28a, Nanos3, Sox3, Neurog3, Pou5f1, and Sohlh1), undifferentiated spermatogonia (Zbtb16 (Plzf) and Sall4), and differentiating spermatogonia (Dmrtb1, Dnmt3b, Stra8, Kit, and Prdm9) were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes at P6 and P8 compared to control (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Genes associated with undifferentiated spermatogonia were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes at P6 and P8 compared to control.
source: However, genes associated with progenitor spermatogonia (Lin28a, Nanos3, Sox3, Neurog3, Pou5f1, and Sohlh1), undifferentiated spermatogonia (Zbtb16 (Plzf) and Sall4), and differentiating spermatogonia (Dmrtb1, Dnmt3b, Stra8, Kit, and Prdm9) were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes at P6 and P8 compared to control (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Genes associated with differentiating spermatogonia were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes at P6 and P8 compared to control.
source: However, genes associated with progenitor spermatogonia (Lin28a, Nanos3, Sox3, Neurog3, Pou5f1, and Sohlh1), undifferentiated spermatogonia (Zbtb16 (Plzf) and Sall4), and differentiating spermatogonia (Dmrtb1, Dnmt3b, Stra8, Kit, and Prdm9) were downregulated in Srsf10-cKO testes at P6 and P8 compared to control (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Srsf10 deficiency disturbs genes involved in progenitor spermatogonia and thus their expansion and differentiation.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Srsf10 deficiency disturbs genes involved in progenitor spermatogonia and thus their expansion and differentiation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on RNA-seq data.

claim: Five distinct spermatogonial subtypes/states were identified in single-cell RNA-seq analysis: USPG1, USPG2, DSPG1, DSPG2, and DSPG3.
source: Clustering analysis identified five distinct spermatogonial subtypes/states as visualized using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP; Becht et al., 2018; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5B showing UMAP clustering.

claim: USPG1 cells corresponded to SSCs.
source: USPG1 cells corresponded to SSCs, as they highly express SSC marker genes, including Eomes, Id4, Lhx1, Etv5, Gfra1, and Smoc2 (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing marker gene expression.

claim: USPG2 cells corresponded to early progenitor spermatogonia.
source: USPG2 cells were highly enriched for Nanos3, Pou5f1, and Zbtb16 (Plzf), with increased levels of Sox3 and Sohlh1, but lower levels of SSC-associated markers and differentiation markers (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), corresponding to early progenitor spermatogonia.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing marker gene expression.

claim: DSPG1 cells are likely late progenitor/early differentiating spermatogonia.
source: By contrast, DSPG1 cells expressed high levels of early differentiation marker genes such as Stra8, Sox3, Sohlh1, Sohlh2, and Dmrt1 and low levels of Pou5f1, Nanos3, and Zbtb16 (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that this cell population is likely late progenitor/early differentiating spermatogonia.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing marker gene expression.

claim: DSPG2 cells are differentiated spermatogonia.
source: DSPG2 cells displayed lower Stra8 expression but mainly expressed differentiation marker genes including Kit, Dmrtb1, Cited1, and Dmrt1 (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), implicating them as differentiated spermatogonia.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing marker gene expression.

claim: The DSPG3 cluster was only observed from the Srsf10-cKO group.
source: The DSPG3 cluster was only observed from the Srsf10-cKO group.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

claim: DSPG3 cells might have differentiated but with abnormal development.
source: These cells express some differentiating markers such as Stra8, Dmrt1, Sohlh2, and Kit, but the expression level of Stra8 and Kit was lower than DSPG1 and DSPG2, respectively (Figure 5C), suggesting that DSPG3 cells might have differentiated but with abnormal development.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the results section based on marker gene expression.

claim: The proportion of USPG2, DSPG1, and DSPG2 subtypes dramatically decreased in the Srsf10-cKO group.
source: By contrast, the proportion in the Srsf10-cKO group was severely slanted, which was manifested by the dramatic decrease of USPG2 (8.1%, 62 cells), DSPG1 (11.6%, 89 cells), and DSPG2 (20.3%, 156 cells) subtypes, and the dominance of the USPG1 subtype (35.6%, 273 cells).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

claim: The USPG1 subtype was dominant in the Srsf10-cKO group (35.6%, 273 cells).
source: By contrast, the proportion in the Srsf10-cKO group was severely slanted, which was manifested by the dramatic decrease of USPG2 (8.1%, 62 cells), DSPG1 (11.6%, 89 cells), and DSPG2 (20.3%, 156 cells) subtypes, and the dominance of the USPG1 subtype (35.6%, 273 cells).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Srsf10 deficiency severely impairs the development of spermatogonia.
source: These data suggest that Srsf10 deficiency severely impairs the development of spermatogonia.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: In USPG1, 184 and 175 genes were downregulated and upregulated, respectively, in Srsf10-cKO samples.
source: In USPG1, 184 and 175 genes were downregulated and upregulated, respectively (|log2FC|>0.25 and p<0.01; Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6A showing volcano plot.

claim: The downregulated genes in USPG1 were mainly enriched for cell cycle, chromosome segregation, mitotic spindle organization, spermatogenesis, and cell proliferation.
source: The downregulated genes were mainly enriched for cell cycle, chromosome segregation, mitotic spindle organization, spermatogenesis, and cell proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on GO analysis.

claim: The upregulated genes in USPG1 were enriched for G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle, regulation of apoptotic process, and negative regulation of cell proliferation.
source: The upregulated genes were enriched for G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle, regulation of apoptotic process, and negative regulation of cell proliferation (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6B showing GO analysis.

claim: Top2a, Mki67, Cdc20, Ccnb1, Ccna2, Cenpe, Rad50, Kif11, Nusap1, and Prc1 were significantly reduced in the USPG1 cells in the Srsf10-cKO sample.
source: Consistently, Top2a, Mki67, Cdc20, Ccnb1, Ccna2, Cenpe, Rad50, Kif11, Nusap1, and Prc1, which are important for cell cycle and cell division, were significantly reduced in the USPG1 cells in the Srsf10-cKO sample (Figure 6B and C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6B, C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dnaja1, Aspm, Ccnb1, Btg1, Racgap1, Sycp1, Sycp3, and Mns1 were significantly reduced in the USPG1 cells in the absence of Srsf10.
source: Dnaja1, Aspm, Ccnb1, Btg1, Racgap1, Sycp1, Sycp3, and Mns1, which are required in spermatogenesis, were also significantly reduced in the USPG1 cells in the absence of Srsf10 (Figure 6B and C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6B, C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The downregulated genes in USPG2, DSPG1, and DSPG2 were also enriched for cell cycle, cell division, and cell proliferation.
source: In the USPG2, DSPG1, and DSPG2, the downregulated genes were also enriched for cell cycle, cell division, and cell proliferation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Depletion of Srsf10 in germ cells likely disrupts the normal cell cycle and proliferation of spermatogonia.
source: These data indicate that depletion of Srsf10 in germ cells likely disrupts the normal cell cycle and proliferation of spermatogonia.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on gene expression data.

claim: Nearly all PLZF+ cells were positive for Ki-67 in both control and Srsf10-cKO testes at P6.
source: The immunofluorescence result showed nearly all PLZF+ cells were positive for Ki-67 in both control and Srsf10-cKO testes (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6D showing immunofluorescence staining.

claim: The number of Ki-67+PLZF+ cells was not significantly different between control and Srsf10-cKO testes at P6.
source: The number of Ki-67+PLZF+ cells was not significantly different between control and Srsf10-cKO testes (Figure 6E), suggesting that all the PLZF+ cells were in the mitotic status.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6E showing quantitative data.

claim: The EdU incorporation was significantly reduced in Srsf10-cKO PLZF+ spermatogonia at P6.
source: Co-staining for EdU and PLZF showed that the EdU incorporation was significantly reduced in Srsf10-cKO PLZF+ spermatogonia at P6 (Figure 6F and G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6F and G showing EdU incorporation assay.

claim: The proliferation of PLZF+ spermatogonia in Srsf10-cKO mice was significantly impaired.
source: These results suggest that the proliferation of PLZF+ spermatogonia in Srsf10-cKO mice was significantly impaired.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section based on EdU incorporation data.

claim: EdU incorporation of GFRα1+ cells was comparable in control and Srsf10-cKO P3 testes.
source: Co-staining for EdU and GFRα1 showed that EdU incorporation of GFRα1+ cells was comparable in control and Srsf10-cKO P3 testes (Figure 6—figure supplement 3), suggesting that the proliferation of GFRα1+ SSCs was probably not much affected at P3.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 3 showing EdU incorporation assay.

claim: The number of CAP3+PLZF+ spermatogonia was significantly higher in Srsf10-cKO testes compared to the control.

evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 6H and I showing apoptosis assay.

claim: The survival of spermatogonia was impaired when Srsf10 is depleted.
source: Double staining for cleaved caspase 3 (CAP3) and PLZF showed that the number of CAP3+PLZF+ spermatogonia was significantly higher in Srsf10-cKO testes compared to the control (Figure 6H and I), implying that the survival of spermatogonia was also impaired when Srsf10 is depleted.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the results section based on apoptosis data.

claim: Srsf10 depletion might lead to abnormal cell cycle and mitotic division, and further affect the proliferation and survival of spermatogonia.

claim: SRSF10 tended to bind exons and was enriched between 0 and 100 nt of the 5' and 3' exonic sequences flanking the constitutive splice sites.

claim: Only 24 genes were overlapped between differentially expressed genes and 1207 targets in LACE-seq data.

claim: Srsf10 has no bias in the regulation of exon inclusion or exclusion.
